subject: GDPR DPA & SCC selection - follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GDPR DPA & SCC selection - follow-up from demo

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — that was really helpful to understand how Redwood handles prefix caching and routing policies. A couple of compliance items we discussed that I wanted to capture and confirm next steps on: 

- DPA: Acme requires our vendor DPA in place before we enable production traffic. Can you share Redwood's standard DPA and confirm what, if any, custom terms you can accept?
- SCCs: For cross-border transfers we need the appropriate SCC module. During the call you mentioned Redwood supports Standard Contractual Clauses; can you confirm which module you propose (Controller-to-Processor vs Processor-to-Processor scenarios)?
- Roles: Please confirm Redwood's typical controller/processor alignment for hosted API and Dedicated deployments. We need this explicitly for our legal team.
- SOC 2: Can you share your latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted is fine) and the date it covers?
- Vendor security questionnaire: We're going to kick off our standard questionnaire — would you prefer a link/form or a spreadsheet?

If you can send the DPA and a short note on SCC module recommendation + controller/processor alignment, I'll loop legal and get back with any redlines. Appreciate it — if it's easier we can schedule a 20m follow-up with legal as next step.

Best,
Alex Johnson
Head of IT Risk, Acme Analytics
alex.j@acme-analytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GDPR DPA & SCC selection - follow-up from demo

Hi Alex — great talking earlier, and thanks for the clear summary.  Below is a concise recap + proposed next steps so legal can triage quickly.

Recap / answers:
- DPA: Attached is our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_v1.3.pdf). We typically accept reasonable data processing term redlines; we can also execute customer-supplied DPA if preferred.
- SCCs: For hosted API and Dedicated (Redwood-managed infrastructure) we recommend the Controller-to-Processor SCC module (the module that maps customer = controller, Redwood = processor). For Private/on-prem deployments the customer controls infrastructure and contracts, so SCCs are typically not applicable in the same way — we can discuss specifics if you're considering Private.
- Controller/Processor alignment: For hosted and dedicated: Acme = Controller, Redwood = Processor. For Private deployments we act as a vendor providing software but customer controls processing; we can provide language for both in the DPA annex.
- SOC 2: Rishi will share our redacted SOC 2 Type II report (covers 2026).
- Vendor questionnaire: Monica will start the vendor security questionnaire — we prefer a shared form (Google Form or secure portal).

Next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Marissa: share DPA + SCC-selection matrix + high-level annex (attached) — by EOD today. (attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.3.pdf, SCC-selection-matrix.csv)
2) Rishi: confirm SOC 2 status and attach redacted report — by tomorrow morning.
3) Monica: start vendor questionnaire intake and send link to Alex — by EOD today.
4) Alex/Acme: loop legal and flag any non-standard redlines. If helpful, propose a 20m call next week to resolve specific clauses.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_v1.3.pdf (standard), SCC-selection-matrix.csv (recommendation grid).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(650) 555-0199

On Jul 15, 2027, at 11:20 AM, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached: Redwood_DPA_v1.3.pdf (standard), SCC-selection-matrix.csv (recommendation grid).

Hi Alex — quick note from security/compliance:

- Controller/Processor: Confirming Redwood operates as a Processor for our hosted API and for Redwood Dedicated (we manage the inference infrastructure). Customers are the Controller for data they supply. For Private/offline deployments where the customer manages the infra, Redwood provides software/services but the customer retains control of processing; we can add tailored language to the DPA for that scenario.
- SCC module: For Acme's use case (Redwood as Processor, cross-border transfers from EU to US), we recommend the Controller-to-Processor SCC module (the standard module used when a controller engages a processor). We'll include the appropriate SCC annex in the DPA.
- SOC 2: We completed SOC 2 Type II in May 2026. I've attached the redacted report (SOC2_Report_redacted_2026.pdf) and a short coverage note. The report covers Nov 2025—Apr 2026 control period.

Attachments: SOC2_Report_redacted_2026.pdf (redacted)

I'll also add a short compliance note to the DPA annex describing data residency and KMS options we support. Happy to join any legal call if useful.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
